The '''Etirhan Independence War''' was a series of military conflicts in [[Etirha]] from 1641 to 1647 that resulted in the country's independence from the [[Merelan Empire]].<ref name="factbook-etirha">{{cite web|url=https://www.theandahfactbook.org/country/etirha/history|title=Etirha: History and Independence|publisher=[[The Andah Factbook]]|date=12 March 1764}}</ref> Part of the broader [[East Atirhan wars of independence]], it led to the dissolution of the Merelan [[Federal Dominion of Etirha|Dominion of Etirha]].<ref name="archives-overview">{{cite web|url=https://archives.etirha.gov.et/independence/overview|title=The Independence War: Overview and Chronology|publisher=National Archives of Etirha|date=4 July 1762}}</ref>

Throughout the colonial period of [[Etirha]], early independence movements had periodically challenged [[Merela Sta|Merelan authority]]. The [[Aeral Sis Risur]], while neither the first nor the last of these uprisings, was the most significant, culminating in violent repression by colonial authorities. The rebellion erupted in response to the [[1621 Etirhan Taxation Reforms|Taxation Reforms]] and was the first instance in which colonial documents employed the term "insurgents."<ref name="archives-aeral">{{cite web|url=https://archives.etirha.gov.et/uprisings/aeral-sis-risur|title=The Aeral Sis Risur and the Language of Insurgency|publisher=National Archives of Etirha|date=19 September 1761}}</ref> The movement also proclaimed the [[Etirhan abolition of slavery|abolition of slavery]] across the Dominion. Historians continue to debate, however, whether the uprising's true aim was full independence or a fundamental restructuring of the colonial social order.<ref name="ahr-aims">{{cite web|url=https://www.andahhistoricalreview.org/articles/etirhan-uprising-aims|title=Independence or Reform? The Contested Aims of the Etirhan Uprisings|publisher=Andah Historical Review|date=2 February 1759}}</ref>

The immediate catalyst for the war was the political crisis of the [[Merelan Empire]] in the late 1630s, when a [[1638 Merelan succession dispute|succession dispute]] and mounting pressure from rival industrial powers destabilized the imperial government.<ref name="factbook-merelan">{{cite web|url=https://www.theandahfactbook.org/country/merelan-empire/succession-crisis|title=The Merelan Empire: The 1638 Succession Dispute|publisher=[[The Andah Factbook]]|date=28 November 1763}}</ref> A public demand for the abolition of [[Irisu slavery]] was ignored.

Early in the conflict, the Dominion of Etirha remained a stronghold for [[Royalist (Etirhan Revolution)|Royalist]] forces, with colonial commanders making effective use of the newly built [[wikipedia:telegraph|telegraph]] network and [[wikipedia:railway|railway]] lines to coordinate rapid troop movements against rebel positions.<ref name="archives-royalist">{{cite web|url=https://archives.etirha.gov.et/military/royalist-logistics|title=Royalist Logistics and the Colonial Telegraph Network|publisher=National Archives of Etirha|date=15 May 1760}}</ref> Merelan soldiers stationed in the capital [[Dazkar]] opened [[fire after protesters]], leading to the [[Rusiguii Republic]] declaring independence in 1641, beginning the Etirhan independence war, [[Etirhan abolition of slavery|banning slavery]] in all forms in the [[Human Rights Declaration of 1641]].<ref name="archives-declaration">{{cite web|url=https://archives.etirha.gov.et/documents/human-rights-declaration-1641|title=The Human Rights Declaration of 1641|publisher=National Archives of Etirha|date=22 January 1763}}</ref> This sentiment of independence spread quickly, occupying most of the Western Etirha by the end of the year.

By 1644, [[Laselteh]] was also at war for independence and became a co-belligerent, opening a second front.<ref name="factbook-laselteh">{{cite web|url=https://www.theandahfactbook.org/country/laselteh/independence|title=Laselteh and the Second Front, 1644–1647|publisher=[[The Andah Factbook]]|date=9 August 1763}}</ref> Aided by continued [[Easuhura|Easuhuran]] support, patriot armies inflicted a series of decisive defeats on imperial forces, culminating in the effective collapse of royalist resistance in 1646.<ref name="archives-collapse">{{cite web|url=https://archives.etirha.gov.et/military/royalist-collapse-1646|title=The Collapse of Royalist Resistance, 1646|publisher=National Archives of Etirha|date=11 October 1761}}</ref> The [[Formal recognition of Etirha by Merela Sta|formal recognition of Etirha independence]] followed with the [[Treaty of Albiran (August 7, 1648)|Treaty of Albiran]] in 1648, marking the end of Merelan sovereignty over the Dominion and the birth of the modern [[Etirha|republic of Etirha]].<ref name="archives-treaty">{{cite web|url=https://archives.etirha.gov.et/documents/treaty-of-albiran-1648|title=The Treaty of Albiran (7 August 1648)|publisher=National Archives of Etirha|date=7 August 1762}}</ref>
